emerging_technology: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) using a language model
intended_application: Draft answers to internal IT knowledge questions for staff review; no autonomous actions
organization: Synthetic Regional Services Co.; no internal production adoption of this application
industry_sector: Midsize regional service organizations in the United States
business_need: Reduce IT support handling time while retaining human review
users_stakeholders: IT support staff, knowledge owners, employees, security reviewer
adoption_posture: Observed conservative adopter behavior: in three prior comparable initiatives the organization postponed operational pilots until at least five of ten matched peers had six months of production outcomes and independent reliability and cost review. It requires these evidence thresholds for this application too; it has the same technical resources and safeguards as the primary case.
capabilities_constraints: Approved searchable documents, retrieval infrastructure, security reviewer and training budget; access-control integration and monitoring unvalidated
risk_consequence_context: Internal information exposure and incorrect answers; mandatory human review, no automated actions, same safeguards in both cases
management_question: When should we begin a trial or production adoption, given the evidence?
time_horizon: Next six months from synthetic snapshot 2026-10-25
additional_context: SYNTHETIC TEST EVIDENCE ONLY; not real-world research. Snapshot S1: 2026-10-25, United States, prior 12 months. E1: Among a defined panel of 100 midsize service organizations, 60 use retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in production for at least one use; application mix unspecified. E2: For internal IT knowledge-answer drafting with mandatory staff review, 20 of the same 100 organizations use it routinely, 30 pilot it, and 50 have not started. E3: Among a nested group of 10 regional service organizations matched on size, IT stack, geography and use case, two use this application routinely, three pilot it, five have not started. Convenience panel: not representative; adoption timing of individual organizations and influential peer networks are not supplied. E4: A comparable controlled pilot found 15% lower median handling time with review retained, but no full lifecycle cost estimate. E5: Target organization has approved searchable documents, retrieval infrastructure, a security reviewer and training budget; access-control integration and error monitoring still need validation. An eight-week reversible shadow trial can run without automatic actions. E6: IT implementation team can support onboarding; vendor supplies connectors but has a sales incentive. No evidence identifies trusted opinion leaders or applicable external standard/certification conformance.
